correctness.rationale: Complete reconstruction over F3 gives thirteen points and lines, 234 noncollinear triangles and 234 tetrahedra, no higher faces. Every forbidden triangle has a vertex cone filling, so the 2-skeleton is simply connected; exact full integer Smith forms d1=(1^12,0), d2=(1^66,0^12), d3=(1^165,3^3,0^66) and zero boundary compositions prove H2=(Z/3)^3 and H3=Z^66. The simply connected 2-skeleton is a wedge of 168 S2, and Smith reduction of 3-cell attaching degrees gives three Moore M(Z/3,2) and 66 S3 summands; the two-dimensional Whitehead/Hurewicz and cofiber steps are explicit. The final package verifier was actually executed and checked on the reconstructed cells. All claims are for the finite 13-point object, not extrapolated.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete homotopy classification of the caps of the smallest odd-order finite projective plane; its three three-torsion Moore components are mathematically substantive, distinguish the object from the known affine nine-point sphere-wedge example, and are invisible in rational homology or arc-size tables. The precise all-caps complex and integral torsion are motivated by finite geometric noncollinearity and topology of simplicial avoidance complexes. No unproved generalizations or research-dominating implications are required for that value.
